name: SysDoctor
author: syswppro

sections.description:
SysDoctor is a read-only connector that links your WordPress site to the Site Doctor monitoring service (by SysWP, at https://sitedoctor.syswp.pro), so you can see what is wrong with a site without ever giving a plugin write access to it.

This WordPress.org edition is monitoring only. It never modifies, cleans, edits, or logs into your site, and never changes your content, files or settings. It reads the metadata needed to spot problems and reports it to the Site Doctor service, where it becomes findings you read in your dashboard. It also keeps its own security activity log (logins, administrator changes, plugin/theme/option changes) in its own database table — the same idea as activity-log plugins — so those events show on your timeline. Metadata only: never passwords, secrets or content.

Built for agencies and freelancers who maintain many client WordPress sites and need a fast, trustworthy answer to “what is going on with this site?” without handing control to a plugin.

What it monitors (read-only)

  • Uptime and downtime — checked from outside the site, with the likely root cause when it goes down.
  • Outdated and known-vulnerable plugins and themes — matched offline against a mirror of the Wordfence vulnerability database.
  • Security changes — new administrator accounts, modified core files, and unexpected changes (detection and alerting, not removal).
  • Performance — render-blocking scripts and the real cause of slow page loads.
  • Contact forms — checked from outside by the Site Doctor service, so you learn if a form stops submitting.
  • Scheduled tasks — whether WP-Cron is actually firing.
  • Change tracking — what changed on the site, and when.

What it does NOT do

  • It never changes your site. No fixes, no cleanups, no file edits, no auto-login, no edits to your content, themes or settings. (It does keep its own security activity log, in its own table — standard activity-log behavior.)
  • It does not send your secrets. This edition transmits plugin and theme versions, vulnerability matches, uptime, performance and change metadata — not wp-config constants, passwords, or post content.
  • It is not a firewall or a malware remover. It detects and reports; you decide what to do and apply any change yourself from wp-admin.

How it works

  1. Create a free Site Doctor account and add your site.
  2. Install this plugin and paste the connection key shown in your Site Doctor dashboard.
  3. The Site Doctor service reads only the metadata it needs and shows the findings. You review them in your dashboard; nothing is ever changed on your site.

Who it is for

  • Agencies and freelancers — keep an eye on many client sites from a single dashboard.
  • Site owners — find out the moment something breaks, and why.
  • Maintainers — a read-only second opinion that cannot itself break the site.

SysDoctor is a connector to an external service, like Akismet. It requires a Site Doctor account, and the exact data it sends is documented in the “External services” section below. Service details and plans are at https://sitedoctor.syswp.pro.

How to use

Once a site is connected, you work with it through the Site Doctor service in one of two ways:

1. Use Doc, the built-in assistant

Doc is the AI assistant inside your Site Doctor dashboard. Ask it about any connected site in plain language and it reads the live, read-only data to answer — no extra setup beyond connecting the site.

2. Connect your own AI

Site Doctor also exposes an MCP (Model Context Protocol) server, so you can plug it into your own AI client (for example Claude) and let the assistant you already use query your sites directly. Same read-only data, driven from your own AI.

Either way the plugin on your site never changes your content, files or settings: it only answers signed requests from the service and keeps its own security activity log.

What to ask

Site Doctor is not only for security. A few examples of what you can ask Doc (or your own AI):

  • Security: “Is this site compromised? Any new administrator accounts or modified core files?”
  • Vulnerabilities: “Which plugins or themes here are outdated or have known vulnerabilities?”
  • Performance: “Why is this site slow, and what is the single biggest thing hurting load time?”
  • Uptime: “Has this site gone down this month, and what was the likely cause?”
  • Database health: “Is the database bloated? Any huge autoloaded options slowing every page?”
  • Maintenance: “Is WP-Cron actually firing? Any scheduled tasks stuck?”
  • Change tracking: “What changed on this site in the last few days?”
  • Fleet overview: “Across all my sites, which ones need attention this week?”

External services

This plugin connects to the Site Doctor monitoring service at https://sitedoctor.syswp.pro. The service is required for the plugin to do anything useful: you opt in by creating a Site Doctor account and pasting the connection key it gives you under Settings → SysDoctor. This is the same model as Akismet and other service-connected plugins.

On the front end this edition makes no outbound calls of its own and runs no background tasks: on your visitors’ page views it does nothing, and it only responds to the Site Doctor service when that service sends it an authenticated request. It makes outbound calls in three cases, all only inside wp-admin and documented below: (1) the connected-site summary it fetches to display on your dashboard, (2) the “Ask Doc” chat, where your question is sent to the service and the answer shown to you, and (3) the optional core file integrity check. None runs on a schedule or affects your visitors’ pages.

Monitoring reads (the service requests, your site responds)

  • When: when the Site Doctor service sends an authenticated request to your site at https://your-site/?syswp_site_doctor_probe=.... Each request is signed with HMAC-SHA256 using the secret derived from your connection key, with a single-use nonce and a ±5-minute timestamp window; unsigned, replayed or stale requests are rejected.
  • Data returned to the service: WordPress, PHP and plugin/theme names and versions; known-vulnerability matches; a list of administrator accounts (login, role and email domain only — never the full address — to flag unexpected admins); indicators of modified or suspicious files and options; performance timings; whether WP-Cron runs; recent server-log digests; and change metadata (what changed and when).
  • Data NOT sent: wp-config.php constants, database passwords, authentication keys/salts, API keys, full email addresses, cookies, session tokens, or post/page content.
  • Legal basis: legitimate interest in site monitoring and security (LGPD Art. 7º IX / GDPR Art. 6(1)(f)). The site owner is the data controller; disclosure guidance is at https://sitedoctor.syswp.pro.

Connected-site summary (your site requests, the service responds)

  • Service: the Site Doctor service at https://sitedoctor.syswp.pro, the same service you connected to.
  • When: only when a logged-in administrator opens the wp-admin Dashboard or the Settings → SysDoctor screen, and only while the site is connected. The result is cached for 10 minutes, so repeated visits do not repeat the call. It never runs on the front end or on a schedule.
  • What is sent: only your site’s identifier (its connection site id, or its group id and this environment’s URL) and a short-lived HMAC-SHA256 signature derived from your connection key, so the service can authenticate the request and return the right site’s summary. No credentials, content or scan data are sent.
  • Data returned to your site: a read-only summary of this site that the service already holds — verdict (open critical issues or all-clear), number of diagnoses, days monitored, events captured, threat alerts, vulnerable plugins, outages, 30-day uptime, actions logged, and when it last scanned — shown to you in wp-admin.

Ask Doc (your site requests, the service responds)

  • Service: the Site Doctor service at https://sitedoctor.syswp.pro, the same service you connected to.
  • When: only when a logged-in administrator types a question in the “Ask Doc” box on Settings → SysDoctor and clicks Send. It never runs on the front end, on a schedule, or on its own.
  • What is sent: your site’s identifier (its connection site id, or its group id and this environment’s URL), a short-lived HMAC-SHA256 signature derived from your connection key, and the text of the question you typed. No credentials, files or content of your site are sent — only your question.
  • Data returned to your site: the assistant’s text answer about this site (drawn from the diagnostics the service already holds), plus how much of today’s per-site limit remains. The conversation is scoped to this one site and capped per day; when the limit is reached you are directed to the Site Doctor panel to continue. The plugin stores nothing and changes nothing on your WordPress.

WordPress.org core checksums (optional, on by default)

  • Service: api.wordpress.org — the official WordPress.org service, the same one WordPress core uses for updates and checksums.
  • When: only when the Site Doctor service requests a core integrity check, and only while the “Check core file integrity against WordPress.org” option is enabled under Settings → SysDoctor. It is on by default; turn it off to keep this site fully outbound-free.
  • What is sent: your WordPress version and locale, to fetch the official core file checksums. No site data, credentials or content is sent. The plugin then compares your core files locally and reports which ones differ from the official release.
  • Terms: https://wordpress.org/about/privacy/ (WordPress.org).

Service links

  • Service URL: https://sitedoctor.syswp.pro
  • Privacy policy: https://sitedoctor.syswp.pro/privacy
  • Terms of service: https://sitedoctor.syswp.pro/terms

Updates to this plugin are delivered through WordPress.org, not from the Site Doctor service. You can stop all monitoring at any time from Settings → SysDoctor → Disconnect, or by deactivating the plugin.
sections.installation:
1. Install the plugin via Plugins → Add New → Search “SysDoctor”, or upload the .zip through Plugins → Add New → Upload Plugin.
  2. Activate the plugin in Plugins.
  3. Go to Settings → SysDoctor.
  4. Paste the connection key shown in your Site Doctor dashboard at https://sitedoctor.syswp.pro.
  5. Save. The site is now connected and read-only monitoring begins. You can disconnect at any time from the same screen.

Don’t have an account yet? Create one free at https://sitedoctor.syswp.pro — add your site and the dashboard shows your connection key.
sections.faq:
Is it really read-only?

Toward your site, yes. It never modifies your content, files, themes or settings — no fixes, cleanups, file edits or auto-login. You apply any change yourself, from your own wp-admin. The one thing it writes is its own security activity log (see below), in its own database table — the same as activity-log plugins such as WP Activity Log or Simple History.

What is the security activity log?

To put security events on your Site Doctor timeline, the plugin records them to its own table ({prefix}syswp_site_doctor_events): logins and failed logins, new or changed administrators, plugin and theme activation/switch, and changes to sensitive options (site URL, admin email, who can register, default role). It stores metadata only — event type, the actor’s login, an IP, and the object changed — never passwords, secrets, full email addresses or content. It only records while the site is connected, and the log is removed when you uninstall the plugin.

What data leaves my site?

Plugin and theme names and versions, known-vulnerability matches, uptime status, performance timings, whether WP-Cron runs, and change metadata (what changed and when). It does not send wp-config constants, passwords, API keys, or post content. The full, itemized list is in the “External services” section below.

Do I need a Site Doctor account?

Yes. The plugin is a connector; it does nothing until you paste a connection key from your Site Doctor account. This is the same model as Akismet and other service-connected plugins.

Does it slow down my site?

No. It runs no background tasks or cron and does nothing on your visitors’ page views — so there is no added page-load cost for your visitors. On the front end it only responds when the Site Doctor service sends it a signed request. Its outbound calls happen only inside wp-admin: a cached read-only summary of this site (sends no site data), the optional “Ask Doc” chat you start yourself, and the optional core integrity check. See “External services” for the full list.

How do I stop it / disconnect?

Go to Settings → SysDoctor and click Disconnect, or deactivate the plugin. Deleting the plugin removes its stored settings via the bundled uninstall.php.

Does it work for multiple sites?

Yes. Install it on each site and paste that site’s connection key. All sites then appear together in your Site Doctor dashboard — built for agencies maintaining many client sites.
sections.changelog:
1.6.0

  • Added “Ask Doc”: from Settings → SysDoctor you can chat with the Site Doctor assistant about this site, without leaving wp-admin. Your question is sent to the Site Doctor service you connected to and the answer is shown here. The assistant is scoped to this one site, reads your diagnostics read-only, and a per-day limit applies; when you reach it you are pointed to the Site Doctor panel to continue. It writes nothing to your WordPress. Administrators only.

1.5.0

  • Added a dashboard widget and a summary on the settings screen that show, inside wp-admin, what Site Doctor found for this site: a verdict (open critical issues or all-clear), when it last scanned, uptime, vulnerable plugins and more. This is a read-only summary fetched from the Site Doctor service you connected to; it sends no site data and is cached for 10 minutes. Right after you connect, it shows that monitoring is active and the first scan is queued.

1.4.0

  • Added a security posture check (XML-RPC, debug flags, registration, file permissions and more) and an administrator audit (admin accounts, last login and detected 2FA plugin). Read-only, metadata only, no outbound call.

1.3.0

  • Added a heuristic malware scan: checks plugin, theme and uploads files for suspicious code signatures (eval, obfuscation, webshell markers, PHP files in uploads) and reports suspects for review. Read-only, bounded, no outbound call.

1.2.0

  • Added a core file integrity check: compares your WordPress core files to the official api.wordpress.org checksums to spot modified or injected files. Gated by a Settings toggle (on by default; turn it off to stay fully outbound-free).
  • Added reporting of available plugin, theme and core updates (read from WordPress’ own update data; no outbound call).

1.1.0

  • Added a security activity log: records security-relevant events (logins, administrator changes, plugin/theme/option changes) to the plugin’s own database table, metadata only, so they appear on your Site Doctor timeline. Removed on uninstall.

1.0.2

  • Polished the SysDoctor logo with a neon glow; refreshed the banner and icon.
  • Fixed the version number shown on the Settings screen.

1.0.1

  • Added a “Connect to Site Doctor” button for guided sign-up (pre-fills this site).
  • New SysDoctor logo.
  • Added a “How to use” section with example questions for Doc or your own AI.

1.0.0

  • Initial WordPress.org release. Read-only monitoring connector for the Site Doctor service: uptime, vulnerable plugins/themes, performance, WP-Cron and change tracking. No write operations.
